subject: Stellara: Tiered discount request + segmented data zone & audit constraints
messages:
From: Aaron Cho <aaron@stellara.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment ask — segmented data zones + tiered pricing

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Stellara is ready to move forward with a Private deployment but we have three conditional asks that impact commercial terms:

1) Segmented data zones: we need logical tenant separation on the same VPC cluster so that PHI datasets and non-PHI datasets are strictly isolated; we cannot accept shared KV cache across those zones.
2) Audit access: our security team requests a read-only audit window (48 hours per year, remote via screen-sharing + logs export) and no continuous tenant-level streaming of production tokens.
3) Discounts: because of the customization and the reserved capacity we plan to commit to, we need a tiered discount schedule: 10% for year 1, 15% for year 2+, with an additional 5% if we sign a 36-month commitment.

I attached a short MAAP request that our procurement team will push through. If Redwood can meet the segmented-zone requirement and the limited audit access, we can prioritize the deal this quarter.

Can you route this to your deal desk and let us know what you can approve at your level?

Best,
Aaron
Aaron Cho
Head of IT Procurement | Stellara Therapeutics
Attachment: Stellara_MAAP_Request.pdf

Team — forwarding Stellara's asks. High level: they want segmented data zones (no shared KV cache), a constrained audit window (48 hrs/year, remote read-only), and a fairly aggressive tiered discount schedule. Procurement attached their MAAP.

Request: can Deal Desk/Legal/LR approve any of these deviations without exec signoff?

Proposed quick positions from me:
- Pricing: approve up to 12% discount on Year 1 with standard ROIs; anything >12% needs SLA/finance signoff.
- Audit: 48 hrs remote read-only seems reasonable but need Legal to confirm wording (no data export beyond logs).
- Segmented zones: Engineering (Priyom) — can we guarantee logical KV separation on the same cluster; if not, what's the delta in ops/cost if we carve out a separate pool?

Attachments: Stellara_MAAP_Request.pdf (from Aaron)

Thanks — Michael

Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment ask — segmented data zones + tiered pricing

Michael / Rishi / Legal —

Summary from Deal Desk POV: Stellara expects three deviations from our standard private template:
- Tenant isolation stronger than our cert: explicit KV-cache separation + network ACLs between zones
- Audit access limited to a short annual window (48 hrs) — they want no continuous streaming/real-time export
- A multi-year, tiered discount schedule tied to commitment length

Commercial ask: they proposed 10/15/20 (with 36mo bump). I'll push counter to 12/15/18 (12% Y1, 15% Y2, 18% for 36mo). Anything above 12% requires exec approval per current delegated authority.

Legal / Security: please confirm whether the requested audit wording is materially different from our template (we typically allow 5 business days with conditions). If it is, flag for Laura.

Finance: if we accept 18% for 36 months, run a quick NPV/ARR sensitivity (handwave ok) and drop results back into thread.

I'll draft the counter-offer language for their procurement team once we have Legal + Eng buys.

—Marissa
Senior Deal Desk Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment ask — segmented data zones + tiered pricing

Michael / Marissa —

Quick technical note: we can guarantee logical isolation between tenant namespaces for model artifacts and KV cache via namespace-level cache keys and enforced routing. However, two practical consequences:

1) Latency: enforcing strict namespace sharding will reduce cache hit cross-tenant sharing benefits; expect a ~5–12% token-latency uplift under bursty workloads compared to shared cache.
2) Cost/Ops: to be conservative we should either provision separate reserved pools (higher cost) or add an isolation flag that disables cross-tenant caching but keeps the same pool (lower cost, modest perf hit). Separate pool increases monthly reserved cost by ~18–25% depending on size.

Audit window: implementing a remote read-only export + sanitized log package is straightforward. We need Legal to confirm what they consider "logs export" (full token traces vs metadata). If they insist on full traces, we need a security review and additional redaction tooling.

I recommend we propose: segmented namespace option (no shared KV) with a performance/ratecard uplift as an optional line item; audit window 72 hrs (gives us breathing room operationally) with log-levels defined in the SOW.

Happy to scope costs if Deal Desk wants numbers.

—Priyom
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, legal-team@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment ask — segmented data zones + tiered pricing

Team —

Thanks for the context and the engineering note. I discussed this with Finance and Legal. Executive decision (conditional):

1) Pricing: approve up to 12% discount Year 1; if Stellara signs a 36-month committed contract we can move to 17% on years 2–3 (total blended outcome to be captured in Deal Desk spreadsheet). Any ask above 17% must come to me directly with Finance rationale.

2) Segmented zones: approve offering an "isolated namespace" option as a priced add-on. Engineering (Priyom) to provide two pricing rows: (A) isolation flag on same pool (no shared KV, lower perf but minimal cost uplift) and (B) dedicated pool (separate reserved capacity — +20% monthly cost). Deal Desk to present both options on the commercial sheet.

3) Audit: approve a 72-hour annual remote-readonly audit window (increased from their 48 hrs to give ops buffer). Log export will be limited to metadata and redacted traces; full token traces not permitted without written CISO-to-CISO agreement and additional redaction tooling + DPA amendment. Legal will draft the exact SOW language.

Next steps: Marissa, send counter (12% Y1 / 17% with 36mo) and include two isolation options + line items. Priyom — please provide the two cost rows by EOD tomorrow. Legal — draft the audit clause and the DPA amendment template. I'll sign off once the commercial sheet and legal redline are attached.

Laura
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redline_v1.docx
